solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Colored arc seen when sun shines through rain
Part of a circle's curved edge
Color of a clear daytime sky
Purple color at one end of a rainbow
White or gray mass in the sky
Hue, such as red or blue

answerNotes.RAINBOW: A rainbow appears when light interacts with water drops. Its curved colored bands are a light effect, not a solid object.
answerNotes.YELLOW: Yellow is a color name rather than a material. The movie's yellow brick road combines a color with a building block.
answerNotes.GREEN: Green describes many growing leaves. It is also a color name in its own right, so read whether the clue asks for a plant or its appearance.
answerNotes.RAIN: Rain is liquid water falling from clouds. Snow and hail reach the ground in solid forms instead.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.SKY: Sky describes the overhead view from the ground. Clouds, the Sun, the Moon, and stars can all appear in that view.
answerNotes.CLOUD: Clouds contain tiny water droplets, ice crystals, or both. Their gray appearance does not mean the water itself is gray.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.

answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.SHORE: Shore is land at the edge of water. It can border a lake as well as the sea.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.

title: Dew on a Meadow in the Morning
subtheme: Dew on a Meadow in the Morning
description: Tiny water drops sparkle on grass as the day begins.
cardDescription: Tiny water drops sparkle on grass as the day begins.
focus: The setting is dew on a Meadow in the Morning. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Water drops forming on cool surfaces overnight
Flat green part of a plant
Small bright flashing point of light

answerNotes.GRASS: Grass commonly covers lawns and meadows. A pasture is land where animals graze on grass and other low plants.
answerNotes.LEAF: Leaves use light to help a plant make food. The flat blade and its veins are useful details to notice when identifying a leaf.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.STEM: A stem supports leaves and flowers. It also connects the plant's growing parts with the roots below.
answerNotes.BEAD: A bead has a hole for threading. A bracelet can repeat bead colors in a pattern or use different sizes for contrast.

title: Pebbles in a Clear Brook
description: Clear flowing water passes over small rounded stones.
cardDescription: Clear flowing water passes over small rounded stones.
focus: The setting is pebbles in a Clear Brook. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Small rounded stone found on some beaches
To move as a liquid in a steady stream
Opposite of deep when describing water
Fine loose grains on a beach

answerNotes.PEBBLE: A pebble is a small stone. Moving water can round its edges over time, giving a brook pebble its smooth shape.
answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.SHALLOW: Shallow means not deep. At a pool, the word describes the water's depth rather than its temperature.
answerNotes.BANK: In a water scene, bank means the ground beside a river or creek. In a money scene, it names a financial business.
answerNotes.SAND: Sand consists of small loose grains. A pebble is much larger than an individual grain of sand.
answerNotes.STREAM: A stream is flowing water in a channel. Brook and creek are other common words for small natural waterways.

answerNotes.GRASS: Grass commonly covers lawns and meadows. A pasture is land where animals graze on grass and other low plants.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.SEED: A seed contains the beginning of a new plant. A seed packet's planting instructions describe how to help it start growing.
answerNotes.STEM: A stem supports leaves and flowers. It also connects the plant's growing parts with the roots below.

answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.
